units.translation: Before Aeschylus, Archilochus used this word in Athenaeus 1 p. 1 f.: ὧν οὔτε τῖμον εἰσήνεγκας [of which you brought no honor].
Where then is the honor which I received in return?
of which you brought no honor

Thus Boissonade corrected for μενειδρεικτείνειν [the manuscript reading].

Thus Meineke on Menander p. 226 and Hermann, comparing Sophocles Oedipus at Colonus 693: πότερα πυνθάνοι᾽ ἂν, εἰ πατήρ σ᾽ ὁ καί-νων, ἢ τίνοι᾽ ἂν εὐθέως; δοκῶ μὲν εἴπερ ζῆν φιλεῖς, τὸν αἴτιον τίνοι᾽ ἂν οὐδὲ τοὔνδικον περιβλέποις [Would you inquire whether your father is the killer, or would you punish him immediately? I think, if you love life, you would punish the guilty one and not look around for justice].
I pay such penalties for my offenses.
before he releases me from these savage bonds and is willing to pay the penalty for this outrage.

so that you may pay requital for the mother-murdering misery.
whichever you found, it remains to pay an equal justice by the spear.
And indeed, if I owed it, I would pay him thanks.
For these things one must pay the gods a much-remembered thanks.
The sons of Priam paid double penalties for their errors.
Still you must, deprived of your loved ones, pay blow for blow.
having paid by death for what he did (thus Naber for ήρξεν).
He said that I would pay these things with my dear life.
But he will pay for the dishonor of his father.
so that he may punish the living dishonorer, the banisher, in the same way by exile.

If then you relax for those who kill each other the rule of not paying and not watching with wrath —.
